capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: Standard Range is the same physical pack as the SR+ with range limited in software (CleanTechnica 2019-05-28). EV Database 2019-2020 SR+: 53.1 kWh nominal (evspecifications lists 52.4 kWh for the North American 2019/2020 car).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: CleanTechnica (2019-05-28) says the Standard Range is the same pack as the SR+ limited in software to about 92 % (220 mi vs 240 mi). Applying that to the SR+ usable 49.0 kWh (EV Database 1177) gives about 45 kWh (49.0 x 220/240 = 44.9).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Standard Range is the same physical pack as the SR+ with range limited in software (CleanTechnica 2019-05-28). Panasonic 2170C cells, NCA cathode, 2,976 cells (96s31p).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: Standard Range is the same physical pack as the SR+ with range limited in software (CleanTechnica 2019-05-28). 357 V nominal, 400 V architecture (EV Database).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Tesla's release note (2020.24.6.4, Model S/3/X/Y) says the car preconditions its battery when navigating to a fast charger; this is a software feature delivered to the whole Model 3 line (2019 SR). Page mentions no manual battery-warming control. A manual control was neither found nor ruled out: Tesla's owner's manual pages were blocked (403) and scheduled-departure preconditioning in search excerpts is cabin-oriented.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: This is an estimate: CleanTechnica did not know how the 170 kW update applies to the base Standard Range; same pack and hardware as the SR+, so the SR+ figure is carried over. CleanTechnica (2019-11-05): software 2019.36.1 raised the SR+ peak to 170 kW (earlier about 100-105 kW). EV Database and evspecifications also list 170 kW.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Tesla service manual says 48 A (about 11 kW) applies only with the Long Range battery and that a 240 V outlet gives 32 A (about 7.7 kW); Basenor/Wikipedia give 32 A for the RWD/standard cars. evspecifications and EV Database (EU, 3-phase) list 11 kW, which does not apply to single-phase North America.
